utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, since we have no technical problems any more, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could one of the technicians assist Judge Nieto-Navia, since his laptop is not working.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would be the second on the list, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two candidates for -- yes. Mr. Usher, I take it that this will be -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, before the witness comes in, the Defence would like to address the Chamber very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Mr. President, Your Honours, the reason why we wanted to intervene is the following: We found that we had grave difficulties with the maps, and not only the Defence has but also the witnesses have. Yesterday, Mr. Ierace said that for obvious technical reasons we should not worry about certain distortions, as it were. But there are certain things that we would like to know for sure so that the witnesses are not confused. And if there is a scale on the map, and I am talking about the incident maps, sniping incident maps and the shelling incident maps, in a sense that there is a scale on these maps, say 1, 12, 500. We would like to know very clearly from the Prosecution what is 1 kilometre. We are told that on this map that the scale isn't correct, neither in the diagonal or in the axis. We would like to know precisely, with a lot of precision, with sufficient precision, what they represent, what 1 kilometre is on the map for 1 centimetre. For instance. We would like to know that in centimetres so that we don't confuse the witnesses. That is, help them find their bearings because otherwise they will not be able to find what they know on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that the enlargement of the maps and sometimes the -- that in the reproduction that you couldn't say for all these maps together how, what distance 1 centimetre represents, because as far as I can see it, some are enlarged more and others are less. There is no scale on that map. As far as the Chamber understands, that both vertically and horizontally, the grid reflects the small parts, 100 metres. And the fixed lines, the blue fixed lines, 1 kilometer. That's how I understood, until now, how this map works and that there is some distortion in the reproduction. If I am wrong, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's correct. The only qualification I would make is in relation to the use of the word "distortion." There is no distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps distortion is the wrong word. If you explain it better.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think you did, Mr. President. I think you explained it accurately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the question that we have to ask, and here I have to base myself on my very vague memories from school. That is about diagonal because we have two axis that one of them is not the same as the other. So the other one was enlarged, the other one wasn't. So what happens to the diagonal because very often we have to make measurements diagonally. So how can we work if we have two different scales. And here we would like to ask Mr. Ierace to shed some light on this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could I assist with that, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By way of background, this may explain thinks. This is what's called an electronic map and it is produced originally from satellite images. The advantage of the electronic map is that when it is placed on a computer it is possible to measure distances between two points with a very high degree of accuracy. When the map is displayed in hard copy form, that is the entire map of Sarajevo, it is possible to reproduce it so that the intersections of the grids create perfect squares. But this is in fact the most accurate way of portraying the map in a small scale in a way in which measurements can be accurately measured horizontally or vertically. The reason that it appears in that compressed configuration is that one imagines one is positioned at the equator looking, in this case, north. Then the compressed latitudinal lines represent the view that one would have of the surface. If it is of assistance to the Trial Chamber, the Prosecution could at whatever stage is appropriate, call an expert to give that evidence in sworn form. I simply give that explanation now by way of background because they may provide some assistance to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I only asked one question that is what should I do with my diagonal. That is very nice to talk about the equator, but are my diagonals correct ones? How can I measure properly a diagonal on this map? Is that possible? Yes or no? I would like to know very clearly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that as a matter of fact that a consequence of what Mr. Ierace told us that you have to be very careful with diagonals, you cannot just measure them. But at least you can say that these diagonals are within a certain scale, that is not less than the small scale and not more than the large scale. But I think you need some mathematics in order to calculate your distances, if they are diagonally, that's how I understand it, and therefore, perhaps measuring diagonally should rather not done on the basis of these maps, although within certain limits one might understand what the diagonal distance would be, not less than, and not more than. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the easiest way to do that is to perhaps take a compass and to place the -- each arm on each of the two points and then with that distance place it on each of the axis and that will indicate the maximum and also indicate the minimum. The distance will be between those two points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One thing is for sure, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that distances on these maps, especially if there are diagonals should be approached with great caution. Mr. Usher, is the -- of course, the Chamber has invited the parties to compromise on maps. I think we have still not been offered one map with -- which shows sufficient precision that could assist the Chamber and which the parties would agree. The invitation still stands. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Nikolic, may I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you have given at the beginning of your testimony yesterday. Examination-in-chief will now continue. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like you to have a look at the map that will be put shortly on the ELMO for you, which is the map of incident number 8. And it also bears number 3. That is the map that we saw yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Ms. Usher. Thank Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, perhaps we could have a view -- no, we can see everything. Witness, do you see the bottom to the right of this map, can you see Bakija, and if you do see it, can you point to it with a pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, what was in this area that you've just pointed to, as far as you know? And I am just talking about facilities that would have been of military interest.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here in the vicinity, but I find this map very hard and not an original. But here in the Bakija in the vicinity, there used to be barracks. I don't know whether it was still there, but certainly there was a facility there. It was a military formations facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. This facility, was it occupied by forces at the time of the conflict? Were there troops there in the facility?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please put your pointer again on the area that you've just indicated where the barracks used to be.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, for the record, the location is more or less where the "K" is below of the name of the proper name Bakija.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what were the weapons that the opposing army had near the barracks?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they fired with heavy machine-guns, mostly with infantry ones, and then below there was a place called Podhrastovi and in that area they had mobile cannons, so to speak. So what they -- that's how they communicated through Bakija and Podhrastovi.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you can you point to this location on the map?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Podhrastovi would be below, there was a hospital there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Below what? Would you please indicate where it would have been, approximately?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below Bakija. It went like this. This is how this road would go, in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is indicating by moving the pointer from left to right an area between Bakija, below Bakija, and three facilities that are black, which are buildings that are more to the left of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when you tell us that there were cannons and that there were heavy machine-guns, was fire opened against us from these positions?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not so often, but, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. As much as you can, could you please answer with a yes or no when it is possible. So when the fire was opened, did you respond?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. More to the right of where it says "Bakija" so going to the lower right corner of the map. Can you tell us what was there, whether opposing position -- the positions of the opposing side?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, I would be grateful if you don't look for actual distance on the map, because we will find it then difficult to work according to your memory. But do you -- could you locate on the map with -- can you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel speak closer to the microphone, please and repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The interpreter didn't hear the end of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you manage --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, on the English language channel, the interpreter has asked Mr. Piletta-Zanin to repeat his question and to move closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think he was repeating his question, but the problem seems the distance to the microphone, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'd like not to be interrupted when there are such problems. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you locate it and point to point number 3.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know where on the terrain itself was number 3 located?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately. I wouldn't know for sure. I wouldn't be able to say precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you can just answer with a yes or no, that would be fine. Thank you. Witness, between the position that you've called "barracks" and number 3 on the terrain itself, what would be the distance between these two points?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly. It would be very hard for me to approximate, to assess.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you perhaps give us an approximate answer?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly between 500 and 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, now could you go back, look at the map, and can you see vertical blue lines? You see them?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to tell you that this blue line, vertical blue line represents the distance of 1 kilometre, we are told. Don't you think that the distance between point number 3 and the point that you've indicated as being the barracks earlier when you said, could it be less than what you've told us?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I told you that I wasn't sure there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like you to point and with the assistance of Madam Usher, could we please see the upper part of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And at the same time, the area -- thank you. Could we just go slightly up. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you. Let's not move it any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please put your pointer on the area of the VRS line which is more to the right of this map.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness indicates the said line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us whether from this line, as far as you know, fire was ever opened in the direction of the barracks?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But when you were responding with fire in defence, was fire opened on the barracks?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, with your pointer can you please point what was the direction of the fire from this line towards the area of the barracks? Once again so that we can see it.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just have to explain that there was a lot of wood here. It was very hard to fire through the wood. So we had to respond to fire without any targeting because the wood was in the middle. We went in these two directions like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness indicates several directions that go towards the south, south-east and south-west, that is, he indicates an area encompassing or around the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, let's go back to the weapons. You spoke to us about heavy weapons. Can you tell us whether BH Army had other heavy weapons in the area that we generally call Sedam Suma, the Seven Woods area?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had mortars, mostly. And from there they fired with the Browning gun on Pale-Vogosca road. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what were the calibres that were at the disposal of the BH Army forces? And I am talking about the mortars.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they used all calibres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, now I'd like you to tell us if you were able to see something in the city of Sarajevo, if you know, what other heavy weapons were at the disposal of the Sarajevo forces in the city itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, objection. Chronology and source of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from that, could you please clarify this. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, yesterday I said that you had 10 minutes left. We are now close to 15 minutes. Could you please conclude soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. This will be my last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As far as chronology is concerned, first of all, if you know anything, can you tell us which period that relates to and on the basis of what experience? Do you have any personal knowledge of this?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I personally experienced certain things, but we also obtained information from people who were leaving the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So what can you tell us about this, please? What can you tell us about other weapons that were allegedly in the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they had a Chinese mortars, at least that's what I heard. They were more dangerous than the local one. They had Chinese hand grenades. You could approach at a distance of 2 metres and launch this grenade and the forest wouldn't be in the way or anything else.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, they were hand-held launchers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Any other weapons?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well we had mobile Howitzers

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I maintain my objection in terms of the source of the information, although he says admissible, this is from unspecified people and one doesn't know what their sources of information were in turn. It is in other words, nebulous to a point that it is not of assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Thank you. I will put this question to the witness again, but I would like him to be more specific because I was speaking about the weapons that the enemy forces had. And in the transcript we can see that it was translated as "we had."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us where you obtained this knowledge of yours from, and when you mentioned Howitzers a minute ago, were you referring to their weapons or to your weapons?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To their weapons. I understood your question correctly. I understood that you asked me about their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. But how do you know this? This will be my very last question.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we know about this because many people remained in Sarajevo and there were exchanges. They would remain down there. They were digging trenches. They were used by the BH Army down there until they ran away, they fled from the town, so we received information in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No other questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, a few moments ago you told us about there being some barracks at Bakija. What were those buildings, how many and how many floors, and built of what material?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building that I saw from above, it was about 100 metres long and perhaps 50 metres wide. It had two or three floors, and I couldn't tell you what it was built of.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did the SRK forces at some stage during the war manage to hit that building with artillery?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, did the buildings survive the war?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, I'll ask you again: Was the building shelled by SRK forces, if the building didn't survive the war?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't shelled. Perhaps it was hit, but I am not aware of it having been shelled. I observed it all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take it then that the building did survive the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there from the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am sorry. I thought you told us that you were in the area of sharpstone throughout the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And from sharpstone did you have a view of these barracks?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I went out into the open at the sharpstone feature, yes, but not from the trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, do you mean from the observation point that you told us about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And based on your observations from that point towards the end of 1995, was the barracks still there?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. In 1995 -- I spent 1995 and the Dayton Agreement period at Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mala Kula being what you described as the Austrian fortress is that correct

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: A matter of what 50 metres from the trenches of sharpstone?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 50 to 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. So did you tell us that when you were at the German fortress for that period of time, you didn't go to the observation point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you in the same company --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is a problem as far as the comprehension is concerned. I don't remember ever having spoken about a German fortress. I don't remember this being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace talked about an Austrian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace, German appears in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I must have said German.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you said German, then I apologise, because I didn't look at the transcript. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, are you telling us that when you were at the Austrian fortress, Mala Kula, for those periods of time you didn't go to the observation point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a guard post. When I was at Mala Kula, I was on guard there. That means that I could have been either at the sharpstone feature or in Mala Kula. I couldn't have been in both places at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many companies in 1993 were stationed at sharpstone? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were ten men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Ten men I take it from the one company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had one company.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many men in 1993 were stationed at Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were never more than five men at Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that mean there were 15 men at Mala Kula and sharpstone at any one time in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, was there always at least one person on duty in the observation point in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One or two. It depended. At night there would be two men and during the day, one man.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And was the company commander typically at the observation point?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would sometimes appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us there were some land lines connecting the observation point to the trenches; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And that is the trenches where there were ten of your company positioned above the ridge, correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sometimes would orders be given from the observation point to fire mortars?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were -- all the trenches were connected. We had the communication lines via an field telephone. So we all listened to the orders at the same time. So all the trenches in the area of the Mrkovici company used one line to communicate. So from soldiers, from security, there would be orders issued to the commander of the company for assistance and to be on the alert.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was Mala Kula also on that same land line?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please take your pointer and circle on the map the area of your company.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates, indicating from the left side of the map, the beginning of the line placed by him in a black marking yesterday, across the top of the map, that is, following the black line, then the broken dark green line, all the way to the compass point on the right-hand side of the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many people were there in your company, let's say in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 70 and 100 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, let me come back to the question you still haven't answered. Did you sometimes hear orders being given from the observation point for the deployment of mortar fire?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were requests from the observation position in the course of combat. If we felt that the enemy side was dominating the situation, then we asked for assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, did you or did you not ever hear orders requesting mortar fire coming from the observation point?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Where were the mortars?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion had -- our Hresa Battalion had a battery or platoon at the rear, but it was in the depth which is where I never went.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see that area on this map?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you mean it is further north?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Higher up, higher up.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You say that the Hresa Battalion had a battery or platoon at the rear. Do you mean a mortar battery?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did they have an artillery battery, that is artillery other than mortars, as well?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am not asking whether you saw it; I am asking whether you knew it?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I take it from an earlier answer, you tell us that you never saw the mortar battery either; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And you told us yesterday you didn't see any artillery at Mrkovici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You went three years in the war at the frontline at sharpstone, sleeping at Mrkovici, did you ever see a mortar?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a 60-millimetre one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. Because if this question relates to Mrkovici, I think that the witness has already answered the question clearly, and I don't think that in this case the question would be acceptable, not in this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question goes well beyond whether he saw mortars at Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question has been answered. I don't think -- I take it that it is not necessary to repeat the question again. No. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you saw within 60-millimetre mortar during the course of the war on the SRK side; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our company, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What else did you have in your company by way of mortars and artillery?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have anything else in our company, apart from that mortar. That was the only piece of artillery that we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As I look again at the extent of the frontline you told us that your company was responsible for, do you tell us for that entire section of the frontline your company had one mortar being 60-millimetres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that you came under attack from the ABiH and they used a recoilless cannon which they set up right in front of Mala Kula and they succeeded in taking that spot and holding it for 30 hours; do you recollect that? Telling us that?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You explained yesterday, you were asked I think three times about it, that you regarded their artillery as being superior to yours; do you recollect saying that?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you say that you were also outnumbered by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Tell me, how then did you manage to retake Mala Kula, since you were out-gunned and outnumbered?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took it, but five men were killed while we were taking back Mala Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Only five; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say only five. It was a large number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what artillery, including mortars, were used in that battle?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have an objection that concerns the tone. I think that to use an adverb such as "only" when people were in combat and experienced combat is not appropriate. It is neither the time nor the place. I would be grateful if one could show more restraint. This is not the right term.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It was entirely appropriate, Mr. President. We are talking about comparative casualties and the credibility of the witness in terms of the evidence he has given as to the superiority of numbers and weaponry of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the accused could keep his voice down. I can hear it clearly from here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General Galic, I know that when you speak, and when you have your headphones on, that you very often use your voice in a louder way than you would do without. So if you approach someone else, perhaps take your earphones off just for a while so that you have better control over your own voice.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I didn't realise that I would be heard. I wouldn't have done this otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... earphones on, so please take care.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. Mr. Ierace, if you could avoid words that certainly have a meaning for you while questioning the witness, but that could be understood also in a different way, and even some people might even say that you could hear some slight sarcasm in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Never, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many SRK soldiers were involved in that assault to retake Mala Kula?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A small number of men came to assist us with regard to the company, perhaps a platoon of about 30 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There were artillery, SRK artillery, at Poljine throughout 1993, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I don't think that we ever mentioned Poljine in the course of the examination-in-chief, and I don't see what the purpose of this question is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, it is not necessary that the questions in chief have covered the area. Mr. Ierace, are you putting this question to the witness on 90(H) or are you putting the question to the witness in order to test the credibility

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, both. Although I would think there was no dispute in Poljine. It certainly hasn't been suggested to any Prosecution witness that there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps that might be clarified. Is that the Defence case, there was no artillery at Poljine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I saw some nodding, but nodding does not appear in the transcript. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is it in dispute that there was artillery in Poljine?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You do not know anything about it. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your, the answer you gave to that question.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Poljine was far enough -- was far from me, the distance between me and Poljine was such that I didn't even know under whose forces it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: There were tanks and Howitzers, were there not, in the SRK that could come to your assistance, if required?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A tank couldn't have come to our territory, and there was no where from where it could have fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you see on the map a road that goes towards Grdonj, at the other end of that road is Mrkovici; isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why could a tank physically could not have gone down that road?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A tank could have gone down that road, but there was no position from which it could have fired. If you have a look at the layout of our positions from the sharpstone feature to Mala Kula and the fortress there was no way the tank would have gone out without it being observed and destroyed by the enemy. The entire line -- the entire line is rocky or it is a forested area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir I suggest to you that tanks regularly fired on Sarajevo from positions where they could be seen when firing from Sarajevo. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they weren't there. I never saw a tank in Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am suggesting to you that the reason you give as to why a tank would not fire from there is unacceptable [Realtime transcript read in error "acceptable"], is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A tank couldn't have fired from any part of Mrkovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, from sharpstone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the sake of the transcript, it reads from there is acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It should be unacceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From sharpstone from the observation point, could you see the flanks of Mount Trebevic to the south?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did you not see firing from those flanks regularly into the city, tanks, and Howitzers?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was firing in Sarajevo on a daily basis. So it was difficult to decide where it was coming from, especially if it was at the end of another town. There was an exchange of fire, there was a crossfire every day in Sarajevo and in the surroundings of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, I am suggesting to you that tanks could be seen firing into Sarajevo from the flanks of Mount Trebevic. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps that's possible. I never saw that. I am testifying about what I know. And this is my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever see an SRK tank during the war?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a tank, but I don't know whose it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, was it close to the frontline? Is that what confused you as to whose it was?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I often went to Pale, Sokolac and the road towards Serbia. On the road towards Serbia I could see a tank or several tanks on the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That was the only one you saw in the whole war, was it?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not the only one. I saw a tank in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, that was -- all right. That was the only possible SRK tank that you saw in the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One or two. I can't remember now. I came across three tanks in the course of the war on the road in all of Republika Srpska and this wasn't covered by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many SRK APCs did you see during the war?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, armoured personnel vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Armoured personnel carrier. I haven't understood you. What do you mean by "APC"?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many armoured personnel carriers belonging to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps did you see during the war?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say how many I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: More than ten?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: More than ten?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's say 10 or 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: One of those would have been very helpful to you and your fellow troops when you were retaking Mala Kula; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. When Mala Kula was being taken the infantry participated in the action. I personally participated in 1993, that was Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the second time that Mala Kula fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say "the infantry participated" do you mean that there were troops other than your company who participated in the retaking of Mala Kula when you were involved?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that we were assisted by about 30 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sorry. I missed that. I didn't hear you say that before. Where did they come from, the same battalion?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't come from the same battalion. It was an intervention platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Within which brigade were they from?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were probably from our brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: See, sir, I suggest to you that your evidence to the effect that you were out-gunned is incorrect, that in fact the Sarajevo Romanija Corps overwhelmingly had the advantage with the numbers of artillery pieces and the types of artillery pieces. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Could the witness leave the courtroom so that I can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, may I ask you to escort the witness for a moment out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, the basis of my objection is the following: This witness is not -- doesn't have a rank. He is not a high-ranking military person, and this concerns the SRK Corps the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and not the company itself. So, first of all, Mr. Ierace should establish what this witness -- what kind of knowledge this witness could have about the entire corps at the level of his -- its artillery, and afterwards, if the witness has any knowledge, then the question can be put to him. Otherwise, the question should be restricted to the line that the -- this witness held, that is to say to the 15 or 13 men that was referred to a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it is important that we know what the basis of knowledge of the witness. If we are talking about the SRK in total, and it is not quite clear to me whether when you say that the advantage, the overwhelming advantage, whether you were pointing at the whole Sarajevo Romanija Corps or just to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps in the area where the witness was on duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, given the nature of the objection, perhaps we should check the transcript. Yesterday for those two occasions, two separate occasions that the witness gave evidence to this effect, on the second occasion, he did so as a result of questioning by Mr. Piletta-Zanin, specifically on that topic, I should add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would you have a word to search for so that we can easily find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I may, my memory was that the questions that I've asked, perhaps there is a problem in the transcript, but they were always in relation to the situation that the witness knew, not with south, south-west. So the questions were always in relation to the line as traced on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, since you are referring to the questioning of yesterday, it is not clear in my recollection. Could you please assist the Chamber in order to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in order to find the -- if you have words then we could search for --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The second reference, unfortunately I only have the page references to yesterday's transcript. I'll read the question. "A minute ago in the course of you are testimony you said that the enemy army had better weapons. What could you tell us about this matter? Could you be more precise? How did you know this" et cetera. So if I have one searches "testimony" or "better" that would bring up that reference --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I am first trying to find the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that what I used in French, was the enemy, the enemy forces, or the opposing forces. That was always in relation to what the witness knew himself in -- about the fighting. And I didn't ask him about the structure of the corps or the weaponry that the corps had or I do not recall asking him about anything to do with the weaponry of the corps or the structure of the corps of the one or the other side and this is where the difference is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I could be given a minute to find the relevant passages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I find a place where the answer -- where the question was: "In the area of the frontline of your company, can you tell us whether you personally knew how BH Army soldiers were armed, what sort of weapons they had?" "Well I don't think I received any information but as I participated in the fighting and mounted resistance --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, can you slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, when I am reading I forget my own speed. I'll start again with the answer. "Well I don't think I received any information, but as I participated in the fighting and mounted resistance, I think that for a long period of time during the conflict, they possessed weapons which were better than ours. They were armed better than we were." What I see is that the question is about the frontline of the company and the answer does not specify. So perhaps it could be clarified when the witness is in again. But you said you had a second reference as well, Mr. Ierace?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I read out the second reference earlier. It came after that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And on that occasion he was asked this: "A minute ago in the course of your testimony, you said that the enemy army had better weapons. What could you tell us about this matter? Could you be more precise. How did you know this et cetera." Answer: "Well, this is something that I felt in combat because we were always attacked by forces that were stronger than our forces and that is perhaps the result of fear too, but we were shelled by the artillery for the most part, so they provided support." And then "is it your testimony that enemy artillery, the BH artillery was its presence was felt more strongly than the presence of your artillery?" Answer: "Yes, that's what I felt."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is still from all these questions and from all these answers it is perfectly possible that the witness was testifying about his own combat experience, and that his answer was limited to the area where he was on duty. So, therefore, it should be clarified, if put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: As you please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience, Mr. Nikolic. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you told us yesterday that the ABiH took Mala Kula on the 14th of June 1993, and today you told us there were two occasions they took Mala Kula. What was the date of the other occasion?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 14th of June 1993, that was the second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was the first time? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which month?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the summer, one of the summer months. It may have been June or July or August.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And which was the time that you helped in its recapture? Was that in 1992 or in June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took part in the retaking in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any artillery support when you did that?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What type of artillery support?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was on the forward position. I think we had mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, and apart from mortars did you have anything else?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not there. There wasn't anything there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there anything in the area by the way of artillery support, other than mortars?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. At least, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there any armoured personnel carriers of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps involved in that retaking?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1993, in June, I do not recall seeing any.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please describe to us in detail the observation point. How big was it?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the sharprock features?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was dug in in the ground of the premises of some 7 to 10 square metres. So this was dug into the rock, into the stone, and the only thing that you could see, there was just a hole 40 by 20, that was the hole towards the city, an opening.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Incidently, for a moment, returning to the topic of Mala Kula, you told us that it was held for, I think you said, 30 hours, or a day or two; is that correct? No more than two days?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I take it it was recaptured, therefore, on the 16th or 17th of June 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And to be clear on this, you say that there were five dead in terms of SRK forces, SRK soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you tell us what infantry weaponry your soldiers had, that is, the 15 soldiers who controlled the frontline as you have indicated on the map, and also occupied Mala Kula? Did you have machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What models did you have?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had three machine-guns of a new production. These were 84 type.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What rifles did you have? What designations? What models?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, what were their designations? What were their model numbers?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kalashnikov, domestic, Kalashnikovs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, it seems that it is sorted out now, but there was a problem in questions and answers. And it is now sorted out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there was a rule a number of times earlier on that these matters could wait until the end of evidence. Does that still apply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It still applies unless it could create confusion. Since Mr. Piletta-Zanin didn't explain to us what it exactly was, I cannot at this moment see whether there would be any confusion. But let's not spend more time on it. The rule is now clear again, and no intervention when there is no risk of confusion. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Kalashnikovs, what else, by way of rifles? Which models?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Automatic rifles, semi-automatic, and automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you have any M-76s?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard of such a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, apart from Kalashnikovs, what else did you have in the way of rifles, along that length of frontline?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Semi-automatic rifles, M-48 rifles. These were old manufacture rifles, apart from Kalashnikov and said rifles and machine-guns and of course hand grenades.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, the position of the trenches was such that they were beneath the ridge line; is that correct? So you couldn't see the trenches from Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first lines of the trenches could not be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. In other words, they were on the other side of the ridge line from Sedrenik to offer protection from enemy forces?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the sharpstone features, that's where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In order to -- I withdraw that. Was the observation point on the slope that faced Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on the slope, but on the actual sharpstone feature itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were the machine-guns set up in relation to the trenches?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to the trenches, they were set up in the trenches. The trenches were dug so that they connected all the trenches and in the event of fighting, there would be fire opened from inside the trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the Chamber would like to have some clarifications as to the observation posts concerned. Could perhaps the map marked by the witness be put -- is still on the ELMO, I take it. During your testimony, Mr. Nikolic, you said that there was an observation post just below the word "Brdo" near to the north-east, south-west. If you are talking about the sharpstone feature, could you please tell us exactly where you situate that on the map? So, sharpstone is the red circle -- yes, at least the line that goes through that red circle --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and other observation posts, you mentioned before an observation post that was taken as well, which is close to the north-east part of the map. That observation post is not sharpstone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was not an observation post. It was a large fort. It was also a former barracks, what I indicated there, below the Brdo, the hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was not an observation post but a larger -- and when you are talking about sharpstone, you are talking about the area just left and just right and through the red circle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the benefit of the transcript, when the witness indicated a fort under "Brdo" he was indicating the top right-hand corner of the map alongside the compass points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I should have mentioned it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you received orders to not target civilians. Who did you regard as civilians in terms of people that you could observe from sharpstone?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians were women and children. Until 1992 -- until the end of 1992, anyone who didn't have weapons was a civilian, because neither side had uniforms. So any armed person represented danger, a risk. And then from the end of 1992, civilians were all those who didn't have weapons and uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that mean that anyone wearing a uniform you regarded as someone who could be shot?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With weapons and going in our direction in the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What about someone in a uniform not carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By "no" do you mean no, you would not shoot such a person?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What type of uniforms in terms of people carrying arms made them appropriate -- made them targets? Are we talking about camouflage uniforms? Dress uniforms? What sort of the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be just fighting at close quarters in fighting. But it would be very hard to see anyone in uniform. They were very well camouflaged. So we didn't have the opportunity to open fire without an attack. We always opened fire only when we were close to each other, in close combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So, if from the observation post you saw someone in Sedrenik wearing a uniform, but not just carrying arms, as you understood your orders, you were not to shoot that person in 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that apply to police officers as well?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If you, in 1993, saw a police officer carrying a weapon, as you understood your orders, would he have been a target?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object. I would just say the setup, in order not to say too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I strongly object to that intervention, the words used by the Defence. It may be appropriate to deal with this matter in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we will have a break anyhow in a couple of minutes, Mr. Nikolic, we have to deal with a procedural issue, but we will then adjourn for half an hour. So Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wish to speak without interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, I would first like to hear more in detail what the objection was about, where Mr. Piletta-Zanin said "setup."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Mr. President. It may be perhaps because I was not interpreted well. What I meant by the setup was the following: This witness said in relation to the soldiers that he -- their orders was to respond with fire and then to target people in uniforms when they were advancing towards them with weapons in a situation. When I said "setup" what I meant without the witness understanding me, is that the question asked by Mr. Ierace was a kind of a trap question because it was impossible to answer that because it would be impossible for the witness to find himself in a situation either it would be a policeman who was turning his back to him and running away or going towards him. So it was really -- I was objecting on the grounds that we believe this to be a trick question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the first point is whether there was a translation problem. I don't know what the French word was that my learned colleague used that was translated into English as "setup." But if there was no confusion in terms of the language, it was highly inappropriate for my learned colleague to say that in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand what you mean that the word "setup" -- first of all, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, spoke in French so perhaps he could tell us what word he used. I was as a matter of fact listening to the English channel at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, my colleagues have informed me that the used in French was "en situation" which has not the same meaning, I would say, as "setup" in English --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. President, may the English booth intervene?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, used the word "mise en situation" he probably meant "context," however "setup" may be also interpreted as being "context." So it could be either. It is impossible for the booth to know what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, you heard the explanation of the English booth, I take it. The French words --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't take it any further because there is, it seems, some ambiguity as to how that word may be interpreted. The effect of it was most unfortunate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not know how these words were translated in B/C/S. Of course, that is what the witness heard. I don't know whether the B/C/S booth could tell us how the words that were in French "mise en situation," context, and in English, "setup," how it was translated into B/C/S for the witness, so that we at least know how the witness might have understood what was said. But now I have some difficulties because now I have to move to the B/C/S channel in order to hear the explanation of the B/C/S interpreters, and that would be on three or two? Six. Yes, I now can hear you in English on channel six. I take it that everyone now has heard the explanation. And I think it is not a matter to pursue at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I thank the booths. I would like to thank the booths. And could we please be very careful with the interpretation details in the future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, we are always grateful to all the booths, and we are always very careful about the language. We will adjourn until 20 minutes past 4.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue I'd like to make a few observations first. If possible, and I urge the parties to cooperate as good as they can, the Chamber would like to finish today's hearing, if possible, at 6.00. It is now -- we would then have not another break and continue for approximately a little bit over one hour and a half. I urge the parties to make that possible. There are important reasons to finish a bit earlier than usual. Then, I have to inform the parties that there was no -- there were no court hearings scheduled for I think the 12th, the 13th and the 14th of December because of the Plenary. There are some initiatives taken to change the date of the Plenary. It is still highly uncertain whether the Plenary will not take place on the 12th, the 13th or the 14th, but if the Plenary would take place in the beginning of December, that would then be the 2nd and the 3rd, perhaps. Well, the second we are not sitting anyhow, but the 3rd of December we are sitting. Then it would not be a good idea not to sit on the 12th, the 13th and the 14th. And I do understand that this is highly inconvenient for the parties. It might be. But I will inform you as soon as I know more about the date of the Plenary. But the parties should prepare if this would be the case, that if the Plenary would not take place on the 12th, the 13th and 14th, that we would sit on these days. I mean, three days lost is just too much. It is with regard that I have to confront the parties with a possible change. Yes. Then, a filing -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin -- Ms. Pilipovic a filing was made today which should have been confidentially -- I again draw your attention to the importance of being very precise as far as protective measures are concerned. That's what I had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as far as the -- yes, I will give you an opportunity Ms. Pilipovic -- as far as the maps are concerned, if these are electronic maps, and if you can look at them electronically, the Chamber -- of course, if they would be available, that's fine. But apart from that, the Chamber of course, will use all maps available, all maps in evidence in order to make whatever determination as to distances, et cetera, et cetera. We are not dependent on one kind of map. But that's, I think, clear for the parties. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Listening to you, Mr. President, I am wondering whether you would be assisted by a map which more conventionally has square grids with the sniping positions on the individual maps transposed to the square grid map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider that, whether that would assist us. And but you also said that in general the map could be produced with real squares on it, not perhaps in detail, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's what I mean. If you wanted it, we could look at tendering a map with the squares -- with the grids --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Grids as real squares --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If that is of assistance to allow you to take measurements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will consider whether we will ask you to produce that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Mr. President, Defence counsel doesn't doubt the capacity of your Trial Chamber to find all of this in all the maps, but what Defence counsel pointed out is that in the case of each witness who has appeared here, this situation was very confused because it was not possible to find on the maps the points that they could remember, themselves. So this is the problem when witnesses are giving testimony. We saw it in the case of this testimony of the witness who spoke about 1 kilometre, whereas the distance was longer on the map. This has to be examined very carefully because this isn't a problem that they are responsible for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it that if mistakes are caused by the difficulties in understanding, reading these maps, that both parties will take care that no confusion will arise and the Chamber, of course, will keep a close eye on that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as translated, that comment by Mr. Piletta-Zanin may well disclose what I would regard as a misunderstanding of the maps. I am happy to meet with Mr. Piletta-Zanin after we finish at 6.00 to explain to him firsthand what the scale is, and if there is a problem after that, then that could be raised in the court tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I appreciate the fact that Mr. Ierace wants to clarify matters for me, but I think that I have expressed myself perhaps badly. I don't think that I have understood something incorrectly. I think that the witnesses might understand something incorrectly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. I don't think that there is any misunderstanding on the side of Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but if the witnesses are confronted with maps which show these differences on the grid and the distances on the grid lines, then that could create some confusion and we are all there to avoid that such confusion will be created. May I -- yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, what concerns me is that if the reference by Mr. Piletta-Zanin in that observation was to the witness stating that he thought the distance between the barracks and point number 3 was 500 to 1.000 metres, whereas in fact according to Mr. Piletta-Zanin's statement it was more, then he doesn't understand the way the scale works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I am afraid, as a matter of fact, that Mr. -- I think that as a matter of fact that Mr. Piletta-Zanin perfectly understands that every grid section is 100 metres, but the grid sections horizontally are, at least on these maps, are a bit longer than the vertical ones, and that whether the witness was misled by the map or that for other reasons he gave the assessment of the distance as he did, I leave that alone for the time being. But I do understand Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that if you say that it was a wrong assessment, it was not more than 1.000 metres, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... perfectly well. Madam Usher, could you then, please -- Ms. Pilipovic, Yes, I promised you to give you an opportunity to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, bearing in mind the fact that you have told us that the schedule might be modified. In the name of General Galic, I would just like to ask you whether we could not have a hearing on the 13th [Realtime transcript read in error "30th"] of December since General Galic has already scheduled a visit with his family -- from the 13th of December. So if we -- if there would be a hearing could that be on the 11th and 12 of December, that would be on Thursday and Friday -- the 13th of December is a Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you are talking about the 13th and not on the 30th --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of December. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... as you know, Ms. Pilipovic, the Chamber is always very much concerned about using the time as efficiently as possible, especially if family visit is there. I don't know for how much time during the day the family is allowed to visit. Could you please give us, not necessarily at this very moment, a small precise information on how many visiting hours are available, how they are scheduled, so that we can try to take as much as we can into consideration --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will inform you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then, Madam Usher, I try now for the third time, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed. And may I remind the parties that setup and upset are words that look very similar. Perhaps it was not perfectly necessary. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In 1993, if you saw a police officer carrying a weapon, as you understood your orders, would he have been a target?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you told us that there was a lot of activity on your part of the frontline in the latter half, the second half of 1993. On the 17th of April there was a ceasefire throughout Sarajevo, was there not?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were very few ceasefires over those days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the 17th of April there was, however, a ceasefire, was there not?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember a single day in the second half of April when there was a ceasefire. Perhaps there was something on paper, but it wasn't respected by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that there was a ceasefire on the 17th of April and that that ceasefire was generally holding on that day. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: VASO NIKOLIC [Resumed]
